# the contributor audit: arbitrary planar extraction and quadratic normal response

Both sources below were read in full and their dependency statements
checked against the already audited finite-support and triangle-cap
lemmas. Both pass. They are auxiliary theorems, not a resolution of OC.

## Arbitrary planar convex-body extraction

Source: `candidate 94bf8f29da63e55b`.

The enclosing triangle uses actual supporting contacts and no limiting
polygon sequence. The support-function erosion argument is valid in
every direction: the inner triangle plus the infinity ball is inside
the standard triangle. All three support orientations follow from the
inner points on both sides of the respective contact. The stated slope,
vertex, inverse-matrix, and determinant estimates give tau<=81 delta.

The strict exterior support representation is exact, and each of its
nonempty caps excludes exactly one vertex because a retained interior
point lies on every edge. Its other two vertices are strictly retained.
Thus the intercepts are positive, below .501, and one is below .01.
Every orientation union is relatively open. Entire different-vertex
unions are disjoint by the single retained edge contact and the two
strict inequalities whose sum contradicts the barycentric identity.
This avoids an invalid uncountable union of null intersections.

The same affine map sends every high-long-coordinate trace into its
own constituent triangle. The strict inequality survives, its image
is measurable, and its area Jacobian gives (64/167)^2 independently
of the number or overlap of the cuts. The loss accounting counts an
own-vertex union once and its two orientation unions at most twice.
Hence sum L_i<=13 tau/10, with each L_i<=tau.

The low-cap lemma applies to every normal, including the separating
endpoint cases: two-vertex caps have a uniform strict area gap, and
the two rational product gaps restrict all other small caps. The
chosen point has all barycentrics above .01 in a whole neighborhood,
so belongs to the actual interior of Q. The product formula, the
large-cap gap, and parallel tightening cover all containing closed
halfspaces. The final difference from tau/180 is exactly
tau(1-404 tau)/(180(1-tau)), which is positive in the stated range.
The nested-body total variation identity and affine invariance are
ordinary continuous identities and introduce no lattice claim.

Both exact verifiers were rerun: the author script passes 108 union
integrals, 1521 tail-map checks, 24 polygons and 2880 caps; the separate
functional audit script passes 7911 checks. The independent full audit
was also read. No additional hypothesis or correction was needed.

## Anisotropic quadratic normal cost

Source: `candidate 09417ac5fa0ac474`.

The seven integer bases and actual convex hull are the audited source;
the small body E_t lies strictly inside T, has area tV, and its exposed
base fibers cannot be enlarged by convexification. The global comparison
with the other anchor maxima therefore applies without a shape limit.

For the relevant triangle projection, the intermediate knot lies in
[0,1/6]. The piecewise quadratic tail has only the zero-shift minimum
or saturation in this range, so the exact paired formula is valid.
The negative-Y direction requires the nonzero-shift minimum; the source
correctly obtains it from the maximum 10/9 of the upper paired law.

The point is localized at g+O(t) before any rescaling. The exact own
cap formula gives excess V delta^2/[9(1-delta)] at g. Its change under
an O(t) point motion is the stated linear term uniformly as delta->0.
Thus any bounded first-order minimizing score forces delta=O(sqrt t).
After the t^(3/4) projection scaling, the point threshold tends to zero,
but the normal becomes (1,xi); the compact shift and null-line argument
is valid for every convergent bounded xi sequence. No normal rate is
omitted or discarded through an unjustified uniform approximation.

The paired lower bound and the competitor xi=eta confine the entire
effective minimization to [-eta,eta]. The objective H has positive
second derivative and its unique stationary point solves the displayed
cubic. Its extra cost Delta is strictly positive. The other two normal
families have limiting paired cost 2 Gamma V at every convergence rate.
The zero-sum optimization yields v=(Delta,-Delta/2), and the exact
global comparison selects base (0,0) for sufficiently small t. The
normalization by 4V+3tV gives the claimed slope7/18+Delta/6.

The author's exact verifier was rerun and passed909 scalar and129
actual-cap/balance checks. These checks supplement the all-normal
sequence proof. No finite-t uniqueness or OC counterexample is claimed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
